title: Launch Agent 7's on-chain Liquidity Layer contracts are specified inside the Artifact itself, not merely referenced
content:
Under the Multi-Instance Coordinator, A.6.1.1.8.2.6.1.2.1.1 commits the Artifact to describing "the high-level design of the Launch Agent 7 Liquidity Layer, including its key smart contracts and their functionality," and A.6.1.1.8.2.6.1.2.1.1.1 carries the addresses of "the Liquidity Layer's constituent contracts" — an ALLOCATOR_BUFFER and an ALLOCATOR_VAULT, the latter labelled ALLOCATOR-INTERVAL-A.

The substantive claim is about where authority over the technical stack sits. By naming deployed contracts in the Artifact rather than pointing at an external registry, the Agent's on-chain configuration becomes governed text: changing which contracts constitute the Liquidity Layer requires a Root Edit, which means an alignment review by the Operational Facilitator and a token-holder vote.

That closes a gap that would otherwise exist between what the Artifact says the Agent is and what the Agent actually operates. Contract-level changes cannot be made quietly as engineering decisions while the governing document continues to describe the old arrangement.

The naming convention hints at planned extension — an allocator vault suffixed INTERVAL-A implies siblings — which is consistent with the Allocation System being the one Supply Side primitive built for many Instances and given a coordinator to manage them.
description: The Allocation System Primitive documents the Layer's high-level design and names its Allocator Buffer and Allocator Vault contracts, putting deployed code under the Artifact's amendment process.
